habit.lifeForm.basis: RHS, of the cultivar: "A large evergreen climber about 3.5m tall". Bean: "An evergreen climber".

habit.climbsBy.basis: Flora of Turkey, as reproduced on the page cited: long shoots usually bear ternate leaves, "petioles twining". RHS, of the genus: "mostly climbing by twining leaf-stalks". Cretan Flora: old petioles "indurate, twisting and clasping".

stem.habit.basis: Cretan Flora: stems "woody, slender", to 10 m long in the wild "but often much shorter".

stem.youngSurface.basis: Bean: young stems silky-hairy. Flora of Turkey: stems "striate or smooth, sometimes hairy when young".

stem.surface.basis: Flora of Turkey, as reproduced on the page cited: stems "striate or smooth". Striate: with fine lengthwise ridges.

stem.youngColour.basis: No flora gives it. Read from photographs: Wikimedia Commons "Clematis cirrhosa var. purpurascens 'Freckles' (54136866406).jpg" (the cultivar) shows the young stems red-purple where they are lit; Wikimedia Commons "Clematis cirrhosa, jardí botànic de València.JPG" (the species) the stems of a season or two red-brown. Bean: young stems silky-hairy, too fine to draw.

stem.oldBark.value: pale brown, fibrous, splitting lengthwise into strings
stem.oldBark.basis: No description of the old bark of this species was found. Drawn as the old stems of woody clematis in general are: pale grey-brown and stringy. To be checked against a plant.

leaf.longShootDivision.basis: Flora of Turkey, as reproduced on the page cited: "long shoots usually bear ternate leaves". Flora Europaea: leaves "simple, dentate or 3-lobed, or 1- to 2-ternate with dentate or lobed leaflets". RHS, of the cultivar: "divided, lobed and toothed". The International Clematis Society calls the cultivar "fern-leafed" and a nursery (https://www.ashridgetrees.co.uk/clematis-cirrhosa-freckles) its foliage finely divided and fern-like, as Bean describes var. balearica, from whose seed it was raised; the photographs of the cultivar read here (Wikimedia Commons "Clematis cirrhosa var. purpurascens 'Freckles' (54136866406).jpg" (the cultivar); Wikimedia Commons "Clématite Cirrhosa Freckles.jpg" (the cultivar)) show broad, toothed and shallowly lobed leaflets and simple leaves instead, and that is what is drawn.

leaf.leafletCount.basis: Cretan Flora: leaves "simple or trifoliolate". Three leaflets where the leaf is divided.

leaf.shortShootDivision.basis: Flora of Turkey, as reproduced on the page cited: "short-shoot leaves simple or rarely ternately divided, deeply toothed to almost entire". Bean: "broadly ovate with a heart-shaped base or three-lobed".

leaf.simpleLobeCount.basis: Bean: leaves "broadly ovate with a heart-shaped base or three-lobed". Flora Europaea: "simple, dentate or 3-lobed".

leaf.margin.basis: Bean: "coarsely toothed". Cretan Flora: leaflets "usually gross-dentate". RHS, of the cultivar: "lobed and toothed".

leaf.bladeShape.basis: Bean, of the simple leaf: "broadly ovate with a heart-shaped base or three-lobed".

leaf.bladeLengthM.basis: Bean, of the species: blades "3/4 to 2 in. long". In metres. Flora Europaea: leaves 2 to 5.5 cm. The cultivar’s own leaf has not been measured.

leaf.bladeWidthM.basis: Bean, of the species: blades "1/2 to 1 1/2 in. wide". In metres.

leaf.stalkLengthM.basis: Bean, of the species: "stalks 1/2 to 1 1/2 in. long". In metres.

leaf.leafletShape.basis: Cretan Flora: leaflets "narrowly ovate, usually gross-dentate".

leaf.surface.basis: Bean: leaves "glossy" and glabrous. Cretan Flora: "glabrous, bright shiny green". Flora of Turkey: "subcoriaceous".

leaf.colour.basis: RHS, of the cultivar: "glossy dark green leaves".

leaf.youngColour.basis: International Clematis Society, of the cultivar: young leaves "light green", mature leaves "dark green".

leaf.winterColour.basis: RHS, of the cultivar: leaves "tinged bronze in winter". Not drawn: the render data gives an evergreen leaf no colour of the season.

inflorescence.type.value: flowers solitary or in pairs in the leaf axils
inflorescence.type.basis: Bean: "Flower solitary or in pairs". Flora of Turkey: "singly or in axillary fascicles". Cretan Flora: "in the axils of clustered leaves, solitary or paired".

inflorescence.flowersPerAxil.basis: Bean: "solitary or in pairs". One is drawn: see the species profile.

inflorescence.held.basis: Cretan Flora: flowers "nodding". Clematis on the Web, of the cultivar: "nodding".

flower.shape.basis: Cretan Flora: perianth "broadly campanulate". RHS, of the Cirrhosa Group: "bell to bowl-shaped single flowers".

flower.widthM.basis: International Clematis Society, of the cultivar: flowers "5-7.5 cm across". The same measure as the growth model’s organs.racemeLengthM, and the unit the flower model is authored in.

flower.mouthShareOfWidth.basis: The width the Clematis Society gives (5 to 7.5 cm) is of the flower as it hangs open. In Wikimedia Commons "Clematis cirrhosa var. purpurascens 'Freckles' (54136866406).jpg" (the cultivar) and Wikimedia Commons "Clématite Cirrhosa Freckles.jpg" (the cultivar) the open flowers of the cultivar are wide bells whose tepals spread at about fifty to sixty degrees from the axis, the tips turned out; their mouth is nine tenths of the published width, which with sepals 3 to 4 cm long is a bell about half as deep as wide. An earlier reading of 0.78 drew the bell too closed beside these photographs.

flower.tepalCount.basis: International Clematis Society: "four sepals". Clematis on the Web: 4 tepals. Clematis have no petals; the coloured parts are sepals, called tepals here.

flower.tepalLengthM.basis: International Clematis Society, of the cultivar: the four sepals "3-4 cm long and 2-2.5 cm wide".

flower.tepalWidthM.basis: International Clematis Society, of the cultivar: the four sepals "3-4 cm long and 2-2.5 cm wide".

flower.tepalShape.value: elliptic-ovate, tapering, the margins somewhat recurved
flower.tepalShape.basis: Clematis on the Web, of the cultivar: tepals "tapering", margin "somewhat recurved". Cretan Flora: "elliptic-ovate". Bean: "oval".

flower.colourOutside.basis: International Clematis Society, of the cultivar: "creamy pink on the outside and creamy white on the inside".

flower.colourInside.value: creamy white, heavily speckled reddish maroon
flower.colourInside.basis: International Clematis Society: creamy white inside with "reddish maroon dots". RHS: "pale yellow flowers ... heavily speckled red within". A garden record of the plant in flower: the "inner reddish-purple spots merging together" (https://fobssheffield.co.uk/plant-of-the-month/clematis-cirrhosa-freckles).

flower.outsideSurface.basis: Bean: sepals "downy outside". Cretan Flora: "densely short-pubescent beneath". Flora of Turkey: "sericeous on the back" (silky).

flower.stalkLengthM.basis: Bean, of the species: flowers "on stalks 1 to 2 in. long". Flora Europaea: "pedicels 2-5 cm". The cultivar’s own has not been measured.

flower.bracts.value: two bracts united into a cup just beneath the flower
flower.bracts.basis: Bean: two bracts beneath the flower "united so as to form a cup-shaped involucre". Flora of Turkey: "2 connate calyciform bracteoles just beneath the flower". Flora Europaea: "a 2-lipped involucre beneath the flower".

flower.bractCupAlongStalk.basis: Where the cup of bracts sits, as a share of the stalk from its base. The floras say "just beneath the flower"; in the photograph of the cultivar cited under flower.mouthShareOfWidth the cup clasps the very base of the flower and of the bud. Read from that photograph.

flower.bractCupWidthM.basis: The floras call the cup "small". In the photograph of the cultivar cited under flower.mouthShareOfWidth it is about a quarter as wide as the open bell and two thirds as wide as a bud, its two bracts running out into points: 13 mm is read from that, not measured.

flower.stamenColour.basis: International Clematis Society and Clematis on the Web, of the cultivar: stamens "green-yellow".

flower.stamenForm.value: filaments flattened, without hairs, longer than the anthers
flower.stamenForm.basis: Flora of Turkey, as reproduced on the page cited: "anthers shorter than the winged, glabrous filaments".

flower.stamenCount.basis: Clematis flowers have many stamens; no count for this species was found. About forty to fifty can be made out in the photograph of the cultivar cited under flower.mouthShareOfWidth; 44 is used.

flower.stamenLengthM.basis: No measurement was found. In the photograph of the cultivar cited under flower.mouthShareOfWidth the boss of stamens reaches a little over half way down the tepals: 19 mm for tepals of 35 mm.

flower.scent.basis: International Clematis Society: a light scent. A nursery: "lightly scented (lemon)" (https://www.ashridgetrees.co.uk/clematis-cirrhosa-freckles).

fruit.type.value: a head of achenes, each with a long feathered tail
fruit.type.basis: Bean: "seed-vessels terminated by plumose styles ... forming large, beautifully silky tassels". RHS, of the cultivar: "silky seedheads".

fruit.acheneLengthM.basis: Cretan Flora: "achenes, 3-5 mm, with a long, persistent, plumose style".

fruit.tailLengthM.basis: Bean: plumose styles "1 1/2 to 2 in. long". In metres.

fruit.acheneCount.basis: How many achenes a head has is not published. In a photograph of the species in fruit (Wikimedia Commons, "Clematis cirrhosa395.jpg", Nanosanchez, 14 February 2013) each head is a brush of roughly thirty to fifty tails; 36 is used.

fruit.colourUnripe.value: green at the achenes, the tails paling to silky cream-white
fruit.colourUnripe.basis: The sources say only "silky". Read from a photograph of the species in fruit (Wikimedia Commons, "Clematis cirrhosa395.jpg", Nanosanchez, 14 February 2013): each young head a hanging brush, green where the achenes are, the tails cream-white.

fruit.colourRipe.value: achenes brown, the tails pale and fluffy
fruit.colourRipe.basis: North Carolina State Extension, of the species: fruit an achene, "brown/copper", "dry small fruits with silky-plumose tail". That the tails dry to pale fluff is as in other clematis and is not stated for this one.

leaf.mainVeins.basis: Main veins from the top of the stalk of a leaflet or of the simple leaf: a midrib, one to each side lobe and a weaker one to each basal lobe. Read from Wikimedia Commons "Clematis cirrhosa395.jpg" (the species) (the large leaves at the top left, whose pale veins fan from the base). No flora describes the venation.

leaf.leafletSideLobeShare.basis: How far a side lobe or big basal tooth reaches out beyond the body of the blade, as a share of the end lobe's reach: about a quarter on the shallowly lobed leaflets and up to a half on the deeply lobed ones in Wikimedia Commons "Clematis cirrhosa395.jpg" (the species) and Wikimedia Commons "Clematis cirrhosa, jardí botànic de València.JPG" (the species); Wikimedia Commons "Clématite Cirrhosa Freckles.jpg" (the cultivar) shows simple leaves with shallow lobes. The middle, 0.4, is drawn and varied by leaf.

leaf.teethPerSide.basis: Coarse teeth on each side of a leaflet between its base and its tip, counted in Wikimedia Commons "Clematis cirrhosa395.jpg" (the species), Wikimedia Commons "Clematis cirrhosa, jardí botànic de València.JPG" (the species) and Wikimedia Commons "Clématite Cirrhosa Freckles.jpg" (the cultivar). Bean: "coarsely toothed".

leaf.faceRiseDeg.basis: How far above level the upper face of a simple leaf looks where its stem lies against the frame: in Wikimedia Commons "Clématite Cirrhosa Freckles.jpg" (the cultivar) (a plant on a trellis) and Wikimedia Commons "Clematis cirrhosa, jardí botànic de València.JPG" (the species) (on canes) the blades face out and somewhat up, their tips a little down. Read, not measured.

leaf.faceRiseOpenDeg.basis: The same where the stem touches nothing: on the free shoots of Wikimedia Commons "Clematis cirrhosa, jardí botànic de València.JPG" (the species) the blades are held flatter to the sky. Read, not measured.

leaf.bladeTurnDeg.basis: How far a blade is turned about its face either way from tip-straight-down: the leaves in Wikimedia Commons "Clématite Cirrhosa Freckles.jpg" (the cultivar) and Wikimedia Commons "Clematis cirrhosa, jardí botànic de València.JPG" (the species) do not all hang alike. Read, not measured.
